title: merge_intervals gives wrong results for unsorted input
issue: `merge_intervals([(5, 7), (1, 3), (2, 4)])` returns `[(5, 7), (1, 4)]`; the expected result is `[(1, 4), (5, 7)]`. Worse, `merge_intervals([(1, 5), (8, 9), (2, 3)])` returns three intervals although (2, 3) lies inside (1, 5). Callers pass intervals in whatever order they were recorded, so the function must not assume they are sorted.

steps.say: I'll start with the module the issue is about.
Before changing anything I want to see what the existing tests cover.
The loop compares each interval only with the last merged one, which is correct only if the input is sorted by start.
Running the tests again to confirm nothing that worked before is broken.

args.summary: The intervals are now sorted by start before merging, so input order no longer matters.
